_what_this_is: SERIES DECLARATIONS. A series name set by the CONTENT OWNER, recorded with the evidence for it and with an explicit member list. Read by engine/preflight_cards.py:name_faults, which compares a DECLARED MEMBER's episode name against the series name, and every other episode against its own page headline (PP-RULINGS A1 / PP-STANDARDS 1a).
_why_it_carries_its_own_evidence: 1a exists to stop the STUDIO inventing a series name so that parts look like a pair -- the EP16 fault, in Jodie's words: 'I was trying to make the part 1 and part 2 fit together, but that is not a thing.' A name the content owner sets is a FACT ABOUT THE CONTENT and is a different thing. But the check cannot tell those apart by looking at a title, and a title typed onto the rail looks exactly like one that was decided. So a series name is honoured ONLY through a record that names its sources and lists its members. No declaration, no citations, no member list -- no exemption, and the EP16 pattern still halts.
_what_this_does_NOT_do: It does not narrow 1a and it grants no discretion. The prohibition on the studio inventing a series name is exactly as absolute as before. An episode that is not a declared member is compared against its own page headline, unchanged. Delete a declaration and every one of its members halts again.
_who_may_add_one: A series is named by the content owner (Hugh). Claude Code records the declaration and its citations; it does not decide one. 1a was ruled by Jodie WITH Hugh on 5 Aug 2026, so an amendment to how it is applied is theirs.
